text:
You need a consistent editor who can turn outlined footage into a polished 15–20 minute edutainment episode with clean storytelling, graphics, and a professional finish for “Rookie to Pro.”

I’m Mina Castellan, and I’d be a strong fit for this kind of structured, story-driven edit. While my background is in data analysis and visualization rather than video editing, the core of my work has been the same kind of thinking your series needs: organizing complex material, finding the clearest narrative flow, and presenting information in a way that feels engaging and easy to follow.

In a recent project, I built a short impact report for Riverbend Education Fund using Excel, Tableau, and statistics. The goal was to turn raw information into a clear story with charts showing attendance and test-score changes for a grant renewal. That report supported a $1.2M grant renewal that was approved. What I brought to that project was structure, visual clarity, and an eye for making information feel approachable without losing substance.

For your episode test run, I’d focus on helping shape the timeline so the teacher/student dialogue and the on-track footage feel connected and purposeful. I’m comfortable with data storytelling, which translates well to building a narrative arc, placing emphasis where it matters, and keeping viewers oriented as the episode moves between explanation and action. I also have experience with data visualization, which gives me a strong appreciation for how overlays, statistics, and on-screen graphics can support the story rather than distract from it.

I’m detail-oriented, collaborative, and used to working from outlines and defined objectives. If you’re looking for someone who can help produce a clean, engaging final product and build a reliable working rhythm over time, I’d be glad to help with the test episode and see if we’re a good fit for the full series.
